strings.name: Coco Gauff
strings.role: Tennis player · Singles and doubles major champion
strings.summary: Gauff drew international attention at fifteen by beating Venus Williams and reaching Wimbledon’s fourth round. Her movement, defense and counterattacking game helped her win the 2023 US Open and 2025 French Open. She also won a French Open doubles title and the WTA Finals. Her development and public engagement have made her a prominent figure in a new generation of American athletes.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: A major champion and leading young athlete, attracting attention in international competition and public debate.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Early training
strings.facts.fact-1.value: Started tennis at six, with coaching support from her father
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Plays
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Two major singles titles
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Came from a set down against Aryna Sabalenka in both the 2023 US Open and 2025 French Open finals.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Top-level singles and doubles success
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Won French Open doubles and the WTA Finals singles title in 2024; reached No.2 in singles and No.1 in doubles.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Eliminated in the WTA Finals group stage
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Beat Marta Kostyuk to finish 2–1 in her group but missed the semifinals after Pegula won the group’s other match.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Another Cincinnati title
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Won Cincinnati and reached finals in Miami and Rome during the 2026 season.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: French Open singles champion
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Recovered to defeat Aryna Sabalenka for her second major singles title after losing the 2022 French Open final.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: First WTA Finals title
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Won the season-ending WTA Finals in Riyadh, adding another major singles achievement.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: French Open doubles champion
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Partnered Katerina Siniakova to win her first major doubles title at Roland-Garros.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: First major at the US Open
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Came from a set down to defeat Sabalenka in New York for her first major singles title at nineteen.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: First major singles final
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Reached the French Open final, losing to Iga Swiatek.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: First tour title in Linz
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Won Linz as a lucky loser, taking her first WTA singles title at fifteen.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Wimbledon breakthrough at fifteen
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Qualified, defeated Venus Williams and reached the fourth round on her major main-draw debut.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in the United States
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born into a sporting family, with parents who competed in college basketball and athletics; began tennis in childhood.
